gloss: running side by side; running parallel

definitions.gloss: running side by side; running in parallel
definitions.explanation: Moving alongside something or someone at the same speed, whether literally (vehicles, runners) or figuratively (projects, processes running concurrently).

examples.japanese: {二台|にだい}の{車|くるま}が{並走|へいそう}している。
examples.english: Two cars are running side by side.

examples.japanese: マラソンの{最終|さいしゅう}コーナーで{二人|ふたり}が{並走|へいそう}していた。
examples.english: Two runners were running neck and neck at the final corner of the marathon.

examples.japanese: {線路|せんろ}と{並走|へいそう}する{道路|どうろ}を{走|はし}っていたら、ちょうど{電車|でんしゃ}が{横|よこ}を{通|とお}り{過|す}ぎた。
examples.english: I was driving on a road that runs parallel to the train tracks, and a train happened to pass right beside me.

notes:
USAGE:
Used for vehicles, runners, roads, train lines, and figuratively for concurrent projects or efforts. In business contexts, {並走|へいそう} can describe running two systems or processes simultaneously during a transition period.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {並走|へいそう}する (to run alongside; to run in parallel)
- {並走|へいそう}{区間|くかん} (parallel section — where road and rail run side by side)
- {並走|へいそう}{期間|きかん} (parallel operation period — during system transitions)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {併走|へいそう}: running together — written with a different kanji but essentially the same meaning
- {伴走|ばんそう}: pacing; running alongside — specifically running alongside someone to support them
